quote: Another major theme is fairness. If genome editing is expensive, it may be available only to those who can pay, or only in countries with advanced health systems. In Australia, a publicly funded health system might make some therapies accessible, but the cost of clinical development is high and pressure to limit expensive treatments is real. There is also an international dimension: wealthy nations could drive research priorities, while poorer countries continue to struggle with basic healthcare, clean water and infectious disease.
reason: The briefing develops concerns about unequal access, private/public priorities, health benefits, need for further research, and safety not being enough, reflecting the core reasoning of the position.
